topics.label: Lecture introduction: cancer evolution, cell of origin, and the microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the fifth lecture in the series, outlining its key themes and learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential mutation accumulation, clonal selection, and epigenetic alterations drive the micro-evolutionary progression of tumors.

topics.label: Stemness, cell hierarchy, and cell of origin in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stem cell properties, hierarchical tissue organization, and specific cells of origin influence tumor initiation and progression in leukemia and intestinal cancers.

topics.label: Microenvironmental influences and stromal support in cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental promoters, inflammatory signaling, and stromal co-dependencies promote tumor initiation, growth, and therapeutic vulnerability.

topics.label: Technological approaches and integrated summary of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss advanced single-cell and spatial technologies for studying tumor cell interactions and synthesize the lecture's overarching principles of multifactorial cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
